highlights.title: What Is Happening to Jobs? Separating AI Hype from Reality
highlights.summary: A Stanford SIEPR policy brief examines the gap between AI displacement fears and measurable labor market outcomes, drawing significant public attention with 264 upvotes and 344 comments on Hacker News. The brief attempts to ground occupational exposure claims in observable employment data rather than theoretical projections. It is among the most widely discussed public-facing analyses of AI's near-term employment impact published this fortnight.

highlights.title: Helping People Choose Careers in the Age of AI
highlights.summary: Steele and Cruz compare six recent occupational AI-exposure projection models, surfacing major methodological divergences in how task automation risk is estimated across professions. They then propose a new empirical framework for evaluating AI exposure that is intended to guide career decision-making under uncertainty. The paper is directly relevant to understanding which white-collar roles face the highest projected displacement risk.

highlights.title: Federal Reserve FEDS Note: The AI Buildout and the Economy — Publicly Available Data to Assess AI's Impact
highlights.summary: Fed economists Soto, Thieu, and Allen catalog publicly available indicators for tracking the generative AI buildout and its macroeconomic effects, organizing them into capacity, adoption, and impact categories. The note provides policymakers and researchers with a timely dashboard of AI diffusion signals, including earnings-call mentions and enterprise deployment proxies. Its framing of 'AI buildout' indicators maps closely to tracking corporate AI adoption rates and earnings-call AI mentions.

highlights.title: Vibe Coding: An Experiment with Test-Driven Development Using LLMs
highlights.summary: Mock and Russo conduct an exploratory study of human-LLM pair programming under a test-driven development paradigm, assessing collaboration quality and output correctness. The findings shed light on how generative AI is reshaping software development workflows and the degree to which human programmers remain necessary as co-pilots. This has direct implications for measuring how deeply GenAI is being integrated into day-to-day knowledge work.

highlights.title: Explainable Reinforcement Learning for Assisting Air Traffic Controllers
highlights.summary: Mehmeti, Gigante, and Venticinque examine how explainable AI can be embedded in high-stakes operational roles such as aviation, healthcare, and autonomous driving to build sufficient human trust for higher automation levels. The study highlights the trajectory toward augmentation rather than full replacement in safety-critical professions, with trust and explainability as the binding constraints on adoption speed. This is directly relevant to gauging workforce AI exposure in regulated, high-consequence sectors.

themes: Occupational exposure models diverge significantly in methodology, making it difficult to produce consensus displacement forecasts without a common empirical standard.
The Federal Reserve is actively building a real-time dashboard of AI adoption indicators, signaling that macroeconomic institutions now treat AI diffusion as a first-order monitoring priority.
Human-AI collaboration in coding and research workflows is deepening, with GenAI moving from standalone tool to embedded co-pilot — accelerating genai-work-adoption metrics.
Trust and explainability remain the primary bottlenecks to automation in safety-critical sectors (aviation, healthcare), tempering near-term displacement projections for those roles.
Public discourse on AI and jobs remains highly engaged but skeptical of hype, with evidence-based policy briefs attracting outsized attention and debate on mainstream tech forums.

watching.title: The Regression Tax: Decomposing Why Skills Help and Hurt LLM Agents
watching.reason: Quantifies skill-addition trade-offs in LLM agents across ~6,000 runs; could inform high-skill wage premium debates as agent capability ceilings become clearer.

watching.title: Federal Reserve FEDS Note: China Shock 2.0
watching.reason: Trade-driven labor displacement from China's export surge may interact with AI-driven displacement, compounding pressure on manufacturing and entry-level wages.

watching.title: Autoregressive EHR Foundation Models with Multimodal Inputs
watching.reason: Clinical AI foundation models advancing zero-shot prediction could accelerate healthcare-admin automation sooner than current displacement curves anticipate.
